nodes.name: Routing engine
nodes.summary: Defines APIRoute, APIRouter, and all helpers that turn a path operation into a live Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) handler.
nodes.detail: fastapi/routing.py is the core of the request lifecycle. APIRouter collects APIRoute and APIWebSocketRoute objects; get_request_handler() builds the per-route async coroutine that reads the body, calls solve_dependencies (fastapi.di), runs the endpoint via run_endpoint_function, serializes the result with serialize_response, and returns a Response. Sync endpoints are pushed into a worker threadpool via run_in_threadpool from Starlette/AnyIO. The module also contains the included-router machinery (_IncludedRouter, _EffectiveRouteContext, RouteContext) that lets sub-routers share prefixes, tags, and dependency lists without copying routes; the frontend static-file routing system (_FrontendStaticFiles, _FrontendRoute, _FrontendRouteGroup) for serving single-page-app builds; Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming via EventSourceResponse; JSONL streaming for generator endpoints; and body-size limiting wrappers delegated to fastapi._body_limit. The file is 6963 lines.

nodes.name: Background tasks
nodes.summary: Extends Starlette's BackgroundTasks with OpenTelemetry tracing so each task is wrapped in an _operation span.
nodes.detail: BackgroundTasks subclasses StarletteBackgroundTasks and overrides add_task (typed with ParamSpec for IDE completion) and __call__. When __call__ is invoked by Starlette after the response is sent, it iterates self.tasks and wraps each call in a telemetry _operation context manager, attributing the span to the task's function.

nodes.name: Concurrency helpers
nodes.summary: Wraps sync context managers for use in async code and manages per-dependency concurrency semaphores.
nodes.detail: contextmanager_in_threadpool runs __enter__ and __exit__ of a synchronous context manager in a worker thread via AnyIO, using a fresh CapacityLimiter(1) so __exit__ never waits for thread capacity. _asynccontextmanager_with_shielded_exit shields an AsyncExitStack's cleanup scope during teardown of async generator dependencies. _DependencyConcurrency holds a max_concurrency int and lazily creates a per-runner Semaphore (stored in a RunVar-keyed WeakKeyDictionary). _contextmanager_with_concurrency_limit wraps an async context manager with a semaphore. run_in_threadpool and iterate_in_threadpool are re-exported from starlette.concurrency.

nodes.name: WebSocket re-exports
nodes.summary: Re-exports WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect, and WebSocketState from Starlette so user code imports them from fastapi.
nodes.detail: This file is a thin re-export shim. All three symbols come from starlette.websockets and are re-exported with the noqa marker so they appear in the fastapi public namespace without being unused imports.

nodes.name: Request handlers
nodes.summary: Functions that build the ASGI callables for HTTP routes and WebSocket routes.
nodes.detail: get_request_handler returns the per-route async coroutine app(request). get_websocket_app returns its WebSocket equivalent. run_endpoint_function runs the endpoint (async or sync). serialize_response validates and encodes the return value. request_response and websocket_session wrap those callables as ASGI apps and inject two AsyncExitStack scopes into the request scope (fastapi_inner_astack for dependencies, fastapi_function_astack for the endpoint function).

nodes.name: Route classes
nodes.summary: APIRoute and APIWebSocketRoute: the objects stored in a router's route list.
nodes.detail: APIRoute extends starlette.routing.Route and adds FastAPI-specific fields: response_model, dependant, body_field, response_field, stream_item_field, is_sse_stream, is_json_stream, form_limits and max_body_size. Its __init__ delegates state setup to _populate_api_route_state and wraps the ASGI app with wrap_app_with_body_limit. APIWebSocketRoute extends starlette.routing.WebSocketRoute and builds get_websocket_app immediately on construction.

nodes.name: APIRouter
nodes.summary: The router class applications and sub-modules use to declare path operations.
nodes.detail: APIRouter extends starlette.routing.Router with prefix, tags, dependencies, response handling fields, and a _routes_version counter. add_api_route constructs an APIRoute and appends it. add_api_websocket_route constructs an APIWebSocketRoute. include_router creates a _RouterIncludeContext, wraps the included router in an _IncludedRouter and appends it, then merges lifespan contexts. The HTTP-verb decorators (get, post, put, delete, patch, options, head, trace) all call add_api_route via api_route. frontend() registers a _FrontendRouteGroup as a low-priority route.

nodes.name: Include router machinery
nodes.summary: The lazy, version-tracked objects that compute effective routes when a router is included.
nodes.detail: _RouterIncludeContext is a dataclass that freezes prefix/tags/dependencies/etc at the moment include_router is called. _IncludedRouter implements BaseRoute and uses a version counter to lazily recompute _effective_candidates when the source router changes. _EffectiveRouteContext is a dataclass that holds the fully-combined state (prefix applied, tags merged) for a single route inside an inclusion; it implements matches() and url_path_for() using the combined path_regex. RouteContext is a frozen public wrapper returned by iter_route_contexts.

nodes.name: Frontend static routing
nodes.summary: Low-priority routes that serve single-page-app static files after all API routes are checked.
nodes.detail: _FrontendStaticFiles extends Starlette's StaticFiles to add fallback logic (index.html for client-side navigation, 404.html for missing assets) and reads the path to serve from the fastapi ASGI scope key instead of the raw path. _FrontendRoute is a single path prefix entry with a _FrontendStaticFiles app. _FrontendRouteGroup collects multiple _FrontendRoute entries, selects the most specific match by path length, and optionally solves a dependency chain before serving the file. The group is stored in APIRouter._low_priority_routes and checked only after normal route matching fails.

nodes.name: request_response()
nodes.summary: Wraps a request-to-response callable as an ASGI app, injecting two AsyncExitStack scopes.
nodes.detail: Modified copy of starlette.routing.request_response. The inner app creates fastapi_inner_astack (for dependency cleanup) and fastapi_function_astack in the ASGI scope, then awaits the wrapped function. If the response was not awaited (indicating a bare-except in a yield dependency swallowed the exception), it raises FastAPIError. The outer app delegates exception wrapping to starlette's wrap_app_handling_exceptions.
nodes.signature: def request_response(func: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response] | Response]) -> ASGIApp
nodes.code:
async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
    response_awaited = False
    async with AsyncExitStack() as request_stack:
        scope["fastapi_inner_astack"] = request_stack
        async with AsyncExitStack() as function_stack:
            scope["fastapi_function_astack"] = function_stack
            response = await f(request)
        await response(scope, receive, send)
        response_awaited = True
    if not response_awaited:
        raise FastAPIError(
            "Response not awaited..."
        )

nodes.name: websocket_session()
nodes.summary: Wraps a WebSocket coroutine as an ASGI app, mirroring the same two AsyncExitStack scope injection as request_response.

nodes.name: serialize_response()
nodes.summary: Validates the endpoint return value against the response ModelField, then encodes it via Pydantic serialization or jsonable_encoder.
nodes.detail: If a ModelField is supplied, it calls field.validate() (or run_in_threadpool(field.validate) for sync endpoints) and raises ResponseValidationError on any errors. The serializer used is field.serialize_json when dump_json=True (the fast path that avoids a Python dict round-trip and uses Pydantic's Rust core directly) or field.serialize otherwise. Without a field, it falls back to jsonable_encoder. Called from the inner app closure built by get_request_handler.
nodes.signature: async def serialize_response(*, field, response_content, include, exclude, by_alias, exclude_unset, exclude_defaults, exclude_none, is_coroutine, endpoint_ctx, dump_json) -> Any

nodes.name: run_endpoint_function()
nodes.summary: Calls the endpoint directly when async, or via run_in_threadpool and _run_sync_endpoint when sync.
nodes.detail: Split out from get_request_handler to make the function easier to profile (inner closures are harder to profile). For coroutines it awaits dependant.call(**values) inside an _operation telemetry span. For sync callables it calls run_in_threadpool(_run_sync_endpoint, function=dependant.call, arguments=values) which runs the function in an AnyIO worker thread.
nodes.signature: async def run_endpoint_function(*, dependant: Dependant, values: dict[str, Any], is_coroutine: bool) -> Any

nodes.name: get_request_handler()
nodes.summary: Builds and returns the per-route async coroutine that handles one HTTP request end-to-end.
nodes.detail: Takes all route metadata (dependant, body_field, status_code, response_class, response_field, form limits, etc.) as arguments and captures them in the closure of the returned app(request) coroutine. The coroutine: (1) extracts endpoint context for error messages; (2) reads the request body (form via request.form(), JSON/bytes via request.body()) checking Content-Type when strict_content_type is True; (3) calls solve_dependencies inside an _operation span; (4) if no errors, dispatches to the SSE stream path, the JSONL stream path, the raw generator path, or runs run_endpoint_function and calls serialize_response; (5) raises RequestValidationError on dependency errors. Uses dump_json fast path when the response class is the default JSONResponse and a response_field is set.
nodes.signature: def get_request_handler(dependant, body_field, status_code, response_class, response_field, ...) -> Callable[[Request], Coroutine[Any, Any, Response]]
nodes.code:
solved_result = await solve_dependencies(
    request=request, dependant=dependant, body=body,
    dependency_overrides_provider=dependency_overrides_provider,
    async_exit_stack=async_exit_stack,
    embed_body_fields=embed_body_fields,
)
raw_response = await run_endpoint_function(
    dependant=dependant, values=solved_result.values,
    is_coroutine=is_coroutine,
)
content = await serialize_response(
    field=response_field, response_content=raw_response, ...)
return response

nodes.name: get_websocket_app()
nodes.summary: Builds the WebSocket handler coroutine: solves dependencies, raises WebSocketRequestValidationError on errors, calls the endpoint.
nodes.signature: def get_websocket_app(dependant, dependency_overrides_provider, embed_body_fields) -> Callable[[WebSocket], Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]]
nodes.code:
async def app(websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
    solved_result = await solve_dependencies(
        request=websocket, dependant=dependant, ...)
    if solved_result.errors:
        raise WebSocketRequestValidationError(solved_result.errors, ...)
    with _operation(name="endpoint", function=dependant.call):
        await dependant.call(**solved_result.values)

nodes.name: APIRoute
nodes.summary: A Starlette Route subclass that holds all FastAPI path-operation metadata and builds the ASGI handler on construction.
nodes.detail: Extends starlette.routing.Route. __init__ calls _populate_api_route_state to set response_model, status_code, dependant, body_field, response_field, stream_item_field, is_sse_stream, is_json_stream, etc., then wraps the ASGI app with wrap_app_with_body_limit. get_route_handler() reads the ContextVar _effective_route_context_var so that an _IncludedRouter can inject a merged context before the handler is built. matches() checks the scope's effective route context so included routes use the prefixed path regex rather than the original.

nodes.name: APIRoute.get_route_handler()
nodes.summary: Returns the request handler coroutine by calling get_request_handler with the route's (or effective context's) fields.
nodes.signature: def get_route_handler(self) -> Callable[[Request], Coroutine[Any, Any, Response]]
nodes.code:
effective_context = _effective_route_context_var.get()
if effective_context is not None and effective_context.original_route is self:
    route = cast(_APIRouteLike, effective_context)
return get_request_handler(
    dependant=route.dependant,
    body_field=route.body_field,
    status_code=route.status_code,
    response_class=route.response_class,
    response_field=route.response_field,
    ...)

nodes.name: APIWebSocketRoute
nodes.summary: A Starlette WebSocketRoute subclass that solves FastAPI dependencies and calls get_websocket_app on construction.

nodes.name: APIRouter
nodes.summary: Groups path operations with shared prefix, tags, dependencies, and response settings; supports nested includes and frontend static routes.
nodes.detail: Extends starlette.routing.Router. Constructor accepts prefix, tags, dependencies, default_response_class, responses, callbacks, route_class, on_startup/on_shutdown (kept for backward compatibility), lifespan, deprecated, include_in_schema, generate_unique_id_function, strict_content_type, max_body_size, and form_limits. It initializes _routes_version=0 for lazy recomputation of included routes, _low_priority_routes for frontend routes, and _frontend_routes for the _FrontendRouteGroup. add_api_route creates and appends an APIRoute. include_router wraps the included router in a _IncludedRouter and merges lifespan contexts.

nodes.name: APIRouter.add_api_route()
nodes.summary: Merges router-level tags, dependencies, callbacks, and response class with per-route settings, constructs an APIRoute, and appends it.
nodes.signature: def add_api_route(self, path, endpoint, *, response_model, status_code, tags, dependencies, ...) -> None
nodes.code:
current_tags = self.tags.copy()
if tags:
    current_tags.extend(tags)
current_dependencies = self.dependencies.copy()
if dependencies:
    current_dependencies.extend(dependencies)
route = route_class(
    self.prefix + path, endpoint=endpoint,
    tags=current_tags, dependencies=current_dependencies,
    ...
)
self.routes.append(route)
self._mark_routes_changed()

nodes.name: APIRouter.add_api_websocket_route()
nodes.summary: Merges router-level dependencies with per-route dependencies, constructs an APIWebSocketRoute, and appends it.
nodes.signature: def add_api_websocket_route(self, path, endpoint, name, *, dependencies) -> None

nodes.name: APIRouter.include_router()
nodes.summary: Includes another APIRouter by wrapping it in an _IncludedRouter with a merged context, and merges lifespan events.
nodes.detail: Builds a _RouterIncludeContext.for_include() that combines the parent router's prefix/tags/dependencies with the include-time overrides. Appends an _IncludedRouter to self.routes, increments _routes_version, forwards on_startup/on_shutdown handlers, and merges lifespan_context using _merge_lifespan_context.
nodes.signature: def include_router(self, router, *, prefix, tags, dependencies, default_response_class, responses, callbacks, deprecated, include_in_schema, generate_unique_id_function, max_body_size, form_limits) -> None
nodes.code:
include_context = _RouterIncludeContext.for_include(
    parent_router=self, included_router=router,
    prefix=prefix, tags=tags, ...)
self.routes.append(
    _IncludedRouter(original_router=router, include_context=include_context)
)
self._mark_routes_changed()
for handler in router.on_startup:
    self.add_event_handler("startup", handler)
self.lifespan_context = _merge_lifespan_context(
    self.lifespan_context, router.lifespan_context)

nodes.name: APIRouter.frontend()
nodes.summary: Registers a directory of frontend static files as a low-priority route at the given path prefix.
nodes.signature: def frontend(self, path, *, directory, fallback, check_dir) -> None

nodes.name: APIRouter.app()
nodes.summary: The core ASGI dispatch method: iterates routes for a full or partial match, then checks low-priority routes, then delegates to self.default.
nodes.detail: Applies form limits from the router scope key, then iterates self.routes calling route.matches(scope). On Match.FULL, calls _route_selected telemetry and route.handle(). On no match, checks redirect_slashes, then calls _match_low_priority for frontend routes. If nothing matches, calls self.default (which typically returns 404).
nodes.signature: async def app(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None

nodes.name: _populate_api_route_state()
nodes.summary: Shared initializer for APIRoute and _EffectiveRouteContext: sets all path-operation fields including dependant, body_field, response_field, and stream detection.
nodes.detail: Shared by both APIRoute.__init__ and _EffectiveRouteContext.from_api_route to avoid duplication. Compiles path regex, normalizes IntEnum status codes, builds per-additional-status-code response fields, calls get_dependant and _get_body_field, detects SSE/JSONL generator endpoints, and resolves the response_model (including stream item type extraction for generator endpoints that return a typed AsyncGenerator).

nodes.name: _IncludedRouter
nodes.summary: A BaseRoute that wraps an included APIRouter, lazily computing effective route contexts and versioning them against the source router.
nodes.detail: Stored in the parent router's routes list. effective_candidates() returns a list of _EffectiveRouteContext | _IncludedRouter, recomputing only when the source router's _routes_version has changed (double-checked locking with threading.Lock). _build_effective_context dispatches on route type (APIRoute, _FrontendRouteGroup, starlette Route/WebSocket/Mount/Host). _match() iterates candidates, sets the effective-route-context scope key for APIRoute matching, and returns the best match. handle() injects form limits and delegates to original_router.handle() after setting the included_router scope key so the router calls _handle_selected.

nodes.name: _EffectiveRouteContext
nodes.summary: A dataclass that holds the fully merged (prefix + tags + dependencies) state of a route inside an inclusion, implementing matches() and url_path_for().
nodes.detail: Built by _IncludedRouter._build_effective_context. Implements the _APIRouteLike protocol so it can be passed to get_request_handler in place of the original APIRoute. from_api_route calls _populate_api_route_state to compute the prefixed path_regex and merged dependant. The app field is set to wrap_app_with_body_limit(request_response(original_route.get_route_handler()), context.max_body_size), built once per inclusion context. The ContextVar _effective_route_context_var is set around the get_route_handler() call so the handler can read the merged context.

nodes.name: _RouterIncludeContext
nodes.summary: A dataclass capturing the merged prefix/tags/dependencies/etc for one include_router call.
nodes.detail: Built by _RouterIncludeContext.for_include() which inherits the parent router's settings and applies the include-time overrides. combine() merges two contexts for deeply nested routers. path_for() prepends the accumulated prefix to a route's path.

nodes.name: RouteContext
nodes.summary: A frozen public wrapper returned by iter_route_contexts that exposes the original route and effective route context via properties.

nodes.name: iter_route_contexts()
nodes.summary: Public generator that yields RouteContext for every route in a router's route list, expanding _IncludedRouter trees.

nodes.name: _FrontendStaticFiles
nodes.summary: StaticFiles subclass that serves index.html or 404.html as fallbacks for single-page-app navigation and reads the path from the fastapi ASGI scope key.
nodes.detail: Overrides get_path to read the path from the fastapi scope dict (set by _FrontendRoute.matches_with_path) rather than from the raw URL path. get_response checks the fallback setting: 'auto' detects index.html/404.html in the directory at request time; 'index.html' always falls back for navigation requests (Accept: text/html); '404.html' always serves 404.html on missing paths. Only GET and HEAD are allowed; other methods raise 405 or 404.

nodes.name: _FrontendRouteGroup
nodes.summary: Groups multiple _FrontendRoute entries, selects the most specific match by path length, and optionally solves a dependency chain.
nodes.detail: _match iterates child _FrontendRoute entries and picks the most specific full match (longest path). handle() solves dependencies via _solve_dependencies (a local async context manager that injects AsyncExitStack scopes) if the group has any, then calls route.app.get_response_for_scope.

nodes.name: BackgroundTasks
nodes.summary: Starlette's BackgroundTasks subclass that wraps each task execution in an OpenTelemetry operation span.
nodes.detail: add_task is re-declared with ParamSpec so type checkers can verify the arguments passed. __call__ iterates self.tasks from the base class and wraps each task() call in a _operation(name='background_task', function=task.func) context manager. The base class __call__ is not called; this override replaces it entirely.
nodes.code:
async def __call__(self) -> None:
    for task in self.tasks:
        with _operation(name="background_task", function=task.func):
            await task()

nodes.name: _build_response_args()
nodes.summary: Builds the keyword arguments dict used to construct the endpoint's Response.
nodes.detail: Takes the solved dependency result and an optional status_code and returns a response_args dict. It always sets 'background' to solved_result.background_tasks so the constructed Response carries the BackgroundTasks instance, and sets 'status_code' from the explicit argument or the response class default. get_request_handler calls it on each request before instantiating the response class.
nodes.signature: def _build_response_args(*, status_code: int | None, solved_result: Any) -> dict[str, Any]

nodes.name: BackgroundTasks.add_task()
nodes.summary: Queues a function (sync or async) to run after the HTTP response is sent.
nodes.signature: def add_task(self, func: Callable[P, Any], *args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> None

nodes.name: contextmanager_in_threadpool()
nodes.summary: Runs a synchronous context manager's __enter__ and __exit__ in a worker thread while keeping async cancellation safe.
nodes.detail: Uses run_in_threadpool(__enter__) then anyio.to_thread.run_sync(__exit__, limiter=CapacityLimiter(1)) inside a CancelScope(shield=True) so cancellation cannot interrupt __exit__. This avoids race conditions when the context manager holds its own connection pool and __exit__ must run regardless of cancellation state.
nodes.signature: @asynccontextmanager async def contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm: AbstractContextManager[_T]) -> AsyncGenerator[_T, None]
nodes.code:
exit_limiter = CapacityLimiter(1)
value = await run_in_threadpool(cm.__enter__)
try:
    yield value
except BaseException as e:
    with CancelScope(shield=True):
        ok = bool(await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(
            cm.__exit__, type(e), e, e.__traceback__,
            limiter=exit_limiter))
    if not ok:
        raise
else:
    with CancelScope(shield=True):
        await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(
            cm.__exit__, None, None, None, limiter=exit_limiter)

nodes.name: _DependencyConcurrency
nodes.summary: Holds a max_concurrency limit and lazily creates a per-runner AnyIO Semaphore to cap concurrent executions of one dependency.

nodes.name: _contextmanager_with_concurrency_limit()
nodes.summary: Wraps an async context manager with a semaphore to enforce the _DependencyConcurrency limit.

nodes.name: _asynccontextmanager_with_shielded_exit()
nodes.summary: Shields a cleanup scope during the exit of an async context manager so cancellation does not abort dependency teardown mid-flight.

nodes.name: _DefaultLifespan
nodes.summary: Lifespan context manager that runs the router's on_startup and on_shutdown handlers when no lifespan= is provided.
nodes.detail: Kept for backward compatibility after Starlette removed support for on_startup/on_shutdown event handlers (ref: Starlette PR 3117). __aenter__ calls router._startup(), __aexit__ calls router._shutdown(). __call__ returns self so it satisfies the Lifespan[AppType] protocol.

flows.name: HTTP request through an APIRoute
flows.summary: An HTTP request is matched, its dependencies solved, the endpoint called, and the response serialized and sent.

steps.text: APIRouter.app() iterates its routes. For each _IncludedRouter it delegates to _IncludedRouter.matches() which lazily builds the effective candidate list (prefix-applied path regexes). On Match.FULL, it calls _route_selected to record the telemetry route label and calls route.handle().

request_response() wraps the handler. It opens two AsyncExitStack contexts in the ASGI scope (fastapi_inner_astack for dependency cleanup, fastapi_function_astack for the endpoint function), then awaits the inner app closure built by get_request_handler.

get_request_handler's inner app reads the request body (JSON or form), calls solve_dependencies (fastapi.di) which resolves the dependency tree and collects validation errors, then calls run_endpoint_function with the solved values.

run_endpoint_function awaits the coroutine directly for async endpoints, or calls run_in_threadpool(_run_sync_endpoint, ...) for sync endpoints, offloading to an AnyIO worker thread to avoid blocking the event loop.

serialize_response validates the return value against the response ModelField (raising ResponseValidationError on failure), then serializes it via field.serialize_json (fast path using Pydantic's Rust core) or jsonable_encoder as a fallback. The response is returned to Starlette which sends it to the client.

flows.name: Sync endpoint offloaded to threadpool
flows.summary: A synchronous endpoint function is detected, wrapped, and run in an AnyIO worker thread without blocking the event loop.

steps.text: During APIRoute construction _is_coroutine_callable(endpoint) returns False. get_request_handler captures is_coroutine=False in its closure.

run_endpoint_function branches on is_coroutine=False and calls run_in_threadpool(_run_sync_endpoint, function=dependant.call, arguments=values). run_in_threadpool is re-exported from starlette.concurrency and uses anyio.to_thread.run_sync internally.

If the endpoint or a dependency uses a synchronous context manager (yield dependency), contextmanager_in_threadpool in fastapi/concurrency.py runs __enter__ in a thread and runs __exit__ in a separate thread inside CancelScope(shield=True), preventing cancellation from aborting teardown.

Back on the async event-loop thread, serialize_response receives the return value. Because is_coroutine=False it calls run_in_threadpool(field.validate, ...) to avoid blocking validation for Pydantic models with slow validators.

flows.name: Background tasks queued and run after response
flows.summary: An endpoint queues tasks on BackgroundTasks; Starlette runs them after the response bytes are sent.

steps.text: solve_dependencies creates a BackgroundTasks instance that is available as a dependency. The endpoint receives it and calls background_tasks.add_task(func, ...) which appends a BackgroundTask to self.tasks.

_build_response_args attaches solved_result.background_tasks to the response_args dict under the 'background' key, so the constructed Response (JSONResponse or custom) holds the BackgroundTasks instance.

After the inner app closure returns the Response, request_response awaits response(scope, receive, send). Starlette's response sends the headers and body, then calls response.background() — which is the BackgroundTasks instance.

BackgroundTasks.__call__ iterates self.tasks and for each task enters an _operation(name='background_task', function=task.func) telemetry span before calling await task(), which dispatches to the task function (sync or async via run_in_threadpool).
